Welcome to Southill Primary
Southill is a happy, welcoming community school where children are known, valued and encouraged to be the very best they can be. We are proud to serve the families of Southill and the wider Weymouth community, providing an ambitious education alongside the joyful experiences that make primary school so special.
We value individuality and celebrate difference, promote equality and make sure that every child has the support and opportunities they need to thrive. We have high expectations for all our pupils and want them to leave Southill feeling confident, successful and excited about their future.
Warm, respectful and trusting relationships are at the heart of our school. We listen to our children, value their voices and work hard to ensure that they feel safe, understood and have a strong sense of belonging.
Our bespoke Bright Futures curriculum is designed to inspire curiosity and open children’s eyes to the world around them. It celebrates our local community and the wonderful area in which we live, while encouraging pupils to look beyond Weymouth, explore new possibilities and develop ambitious dreams for their futures.
Alongside strong academic foundations, we nurture creativity, teamwork, kindness, empathy and resilience. We place great importance on physical and mental wellbeing, helping our children to become happy, confident and prepared young people.
Matt Ryan | Acting Headteacher

Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club is BRILL! In addition to offering a nutritious and filling breakfast with a choice of cereals, toast, fruit and yoghurt - on some days we even have pancakes and crumpets! Children enjoy different activities every day including skipping, table tennis, board games, puzzles, Lego, colouring and books. It’s a great way to start the day!
Each session runs from 7.45 am and the current cost is £4.50, spaces are available on a weekly basis, we support regular working patterns and also families who might only require the occasional day or sessions with little notice.
For more info, contact the school office at office@southill.dorset.sch.uk
After School Club
The Kool Kidz Club is a registered After School Club, which provides a collection service from Southill Primary. They cater for children aged 4 years and up to 11 years until the end of primary education.
The Club offers a happy and relaxed atmosphere within a safe and stimulating environment maintained by qualified, experienced, and friendly staff. Kool Kidz provide a wide variety of activities with excellent equipment and resources for the children to enjoy. They also benefit from use of the school's outside facilities.
The After School Club operates from 3.15pm until 5.30pm. Snacks and refreshments are provided.
The Kool Kidz Club is a separate entity to Southill Primary but located on our site and collect from our school hall.
For more information, see their website: https://www.humptyshousepreschool.co.uk/?page_id=24

Learning a foreign language is a necessary part of being a member of a multi-cultural society and provides an opening to other cultures. A high-quality languages education should foster children’s curiosity and deepen their understanding of the world.
It is our intent that the Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) curriculum at Southill primary School will provide children with the skills and knowledge to confidently communicate in a language other than their own. The curriculum will enable children to express their ideas and thoughts in another language and to understand and respond to its speakers, both in speech and in writing. It will also provide opportunities for them to read great literature in the original language.
It is intended that when children leave Southill Primary School, they will have a natural curiosity and confidence to explore other countries, cultures and languages. They will accept that in a multi-lingual society, it is a valuable skill to be able to communicate effectively with others in another language. They will be engaged and prepared to continue language learning further in their future education and beyond.

Reception's Final Full Week – Ready for Year 1!
What a fantastic final full week we have had in Reception! It has been wonderful to look back at just how much the children have grown in confidence, independence and ability over the year. This week has been full of exciting activities that have celebrated all of the amazing skills the children have developed as they prepare for their next big adventure in Year 1.
In maths, we have been practising writing our numbers neatly inside squares, helping us to develop the presentation and accuracy needed for Year 1. The children showed fantastic concentration and determination, taking great pride in making sure their numbers were carefully formed.
Our fine motor skills have continued to flourish as we have spent time improving our cutting skills. From carefully following lines to cutting out shapes with increasing precision, the children have demonstrated just how much their hand strength and control have improved since September.
Reading has remained a big focus this week, with the children enjoying sharing books together, using their phonics knowledge to decode unfamiliar words and developing their confidence and fluency. It has been lovely to see their enthusiasm for stories and the pride they take in reading independently.
The children have also been working hard on their writing, using their phonics, spelling knowledge and sentence skills to write independently. They have been remembering capital letters, finger spaces and full stops, creating wonderful sentences that show just how ready they are for the expectations of Year 1.
Our imaginative play has been just as busy! The dolls' house has inspired some fantastic storytelling, with the children creating their own characters, adventures and exciting endings. It has been wonderful to listen to their conversations as they developed their vocabulary, communication skills and creativity through play.
As we come to the end of our final full week in Reception, we are incredibly proud of everything the children have achieved. They have worked so hard, supported one another, shown kindness and resilience, and embraced every challenge with enthusiasm. Watching their confidence blossom throughout the year has been a real privilege.
We have thoroughly enjoyed making special memories together during our last few weeks in Reception and are so excited to see the children take their next steps into Year 1. We know they are more than ready for the adventure ahead, and we cannot wait to see all the wonderful things they will achieve next.
Well done, Reception—you have been amazing!

Science – Exploring Sound
Year 4 Science - Sound
In Science, Year 4 have been learning about sound. Yesterday, our lesson focused on pitch and how it is different from volume.
To support their understanding, the children made their own pan flutes using tubes of different lengths. They quickly discovered that shorter tubes produced higher-pitched sounds, while longer tubes produced lower-pitched sounds.
As they investigated, the classroom was filled with excited observations. We heard comments such as, "This tube makes a really high sound because it's shorter!", "The longer tube sounds much lower," and "If I blow harder, it gets louder, but the pitch stays the same!" These discussions showed that the children were beginning to understand the difference between pitch (how high or low a sound is) and volume (how loud or quiet a sound is).
The children also experimented with blowing gently and more strongly into their pan flutes. They realised that blowing harder made the sound louder, but it did not change the pitch.
It was wonderful to see the children working collaboratively, testing their ideas, making predictions and explaining their thinking using scientific vocabulary. They thoroughly enjoyed this practical investigation and were proud of the musical instruments they had created!

Friends of Southill School
Why we love FOSS
The children of Southill Primary School are very lucky to be supported by our hard-working Parent and Teacher Association, who we call Friends of Southill School (FOSS).
You might not realise, but all parents/carers are automatically members of FOSS. This is good for the school and our children because it means that we can have closer and more effective links with parents via the events that FOSS organise and the fundraising that they do for our school.
A thriving PTA is essential for any good school. Not only do FOSS provide an opportunity for parents, carers and families to get together, FOSS also raises vital funds for Southill Primary. Dorset is one of the lowest funded authorities in the country, so any help with the purchase of exciting extras for our children is always warmly welcome.
Without this support, many regular trips, visits and events would not be able to go ahead. Every class trip is subsidised from FOSS funds to make them more affordable for parents. Each class benefits from an annual donation, too. FOSS organise discos, an annual Spring Trail and our much-anticipated Christmas and Spring Fayres – all offering the chance to pull together as a school and to do something lovely for the good of our pupils.
FOSS really is fantastic, volunteering is fun and extremely rewarding. No matter how small your input – you can be sure to make a big impact! Parents, carers and family members are always welcome to join to help our school. They are not a large intimidating organisation by any means; they are a friendly, enthusiastic group of people who enjoy getting involved. If you would like to take part, feel free to get in touch at FOSS@southill.dorset.sch.uk or find them on their Facebook page. They’d love to hear from you!

School Uniform
It is our policy that all children should wear school uniform when attending school, or when participating in a school-organised event outside normal school hours. We respectfully request that before purchasing any item that is not specifically listed that you check with school to ensure suitability. It is our aim to keep our uniform consistent. We ask that all parents support our effort to make all aspects of our school outstanding and we believe, as far as possible, a strict adherence to our uniform policy helps.
At Southill, we believe that a school uniform:
engenders a feeling of community and belonging;
supports positive behaviour and discipline;
is practical and smart;
The Role of Parents/Carers
We ask all parents who send their children to our school to support the school uniform policy.
Southill Primary welcomes children from all backgrounds and faith communities. If there are strong reasons, e.g. on religious grounds, why parents would like their child to wear clothes that differ from school uniform, the school will give consideration to such requests. Similarly, should an item of school uniform prove problematic for a pupil with disabilities, parents are invited to draw this to the attention of the headteacher.
The Role of Governors
The governing body supports the headteacher in implementing the school uniform policy, and liaises with the headteacher to ensure that the policy is implemented fairly and with sensitivity. It is the governors’ responsibility to ensure the school uniform meets all national regulations concerning equal opportunities, and that our school uniform policy is consistent with our policy on equal opportunities. Governors ensure that the school uniform policy helps children to dress sensibly, in clothing that is hardwearing, safe and practical.
Clothing Grant
School can provide assistance for uniform. The Governors have decided that the criteria for this assistance is that parents must be entitled to free school meals for their child. Vouchers will be provided for purchase of school uniform during the school year. For further information, please contact the office staff.
Second-hand uniform
Second-hand uniforms can benefit all parents, not just those on lower incomes. It is also better for the planet, as selling uniform in this way can extend the life of garments and therefore cut down on waste. We are able to supply second-hand uniform through FOSS, the friends of Southill School. You can contact them about this in a number of ways:
through the school office

through the FOSS events website
Uniform Guidance
Jewellery
On health and safety grounds we do not allow children to wear jewellery in our school, except for watches and small ear-studs.
Rec/KS1 (up to and including Year 2) children should not wear any earrings to school – if you do wish to have your child’s ears pierced, please wait until the summer break so they have time to heal.
KS2 (Years 3, 4, 5 and 6) children may wear simple, small studs. These must be removed by the child before P.E.
Hairstyles
The school aims to maintain a focused learning environment, so we kindly ask that children’s hairstyles do not become a distraction to others. Parents are reminded that hair braids with beads are not allowed, and hair should be kept in natural colours. For those with long hair, please ensure it is tied up using small and simple accessories such as ribbons, bows, bobbles, hair bands or slides. For short hair, we request that it remains neat and tidy. While we do not require specific styles or lengths, we ask that you avoid tramlines or shapes cut into the hair.
Footwear
All children are required to wear plain black shoes. This helps maintain uniformity and reduces competitiveness related to branded footwear. Trainers and canvas shoes are not permitted (except on PE days). To ensure the safety and wellbeing of our pupils, shoes with platform soles, open-toed sandals, or high heels are not allowed. These styles can pose safety risks during school activities. During the winter months, plain black boots are acceptable. This ensures that children are comfortable and warm while adhering to our uniform policy. We encourage all pupils to wear practical shoes that are well-maintained. This reflects our commitment to a smart appearance and instills pride in our school identity.

Reading: Our Greatest Strength
We are immensely proud of our vibrant, inclusive reading culture where every child develops into a confident, enthusiastic and independent reader who genuinely loves books.
Reading unlocks learning across our entire curriculum, broadens horizons and nurtures a lifelong love of literature. Through our carefully designed reading curriculum and the rich experiences we provide, we:
Building Strong Foundations from the Start
Children start to learn to read with Little Wandle Phonics as soon as they start school. This systematic synthetic phonics programme provides a structured and consistent approach that ensures every child develops the essential skills they need to become confident readers.
Our commitment to excellence in early reading is reflected in our Phonics Screening Check results, which are exceptionally high – always above 90%. This outstanding achievement demonstrates that our children are developing strong foundational reading skills that will support them throughout their education and beyond.

Weekly Celebrations
Every week in assembly, we celebrate our dedicated readers, recognising their commitment and achievements. This regular recognition reinforces that reading matters at Southill and motivates all our children to develop their reading habits.

We are proud to collaborate with The Rebel Reading Society to excite and motivate our readers. Our Rebel Readers meet every week, creating a community of enthusiastic readers who inspire others and drive our reading culture forward.
Our Library
All classes visit our beautiful library every week, ensuring that reading is prioritised across the school. We invest heavily in the latest titles, ensuring our children have access to contemporary, engaging books that reflect their interests and the world around them.
Book Week
Our jam-packed Book Week is a highlight of the school year, featuring a myriad of events that bring stories to life and celebrate reading in all its forms. From author visits to creative activities, every child experiences the joy and excitement that books can bring.

We compete in the National Reading Championships every year, challenging our pupils and celebrating their reading achievements on a national stage. This demonstrates our commitment to excellence and gives our children the opportunity to showcase their reading skills.
